headline: RBI tightens card tokenisation rules for recurring and offline payments

sections.heading: What happened
sections.body: The Reserve Bank of India issued updated directions on security in card-based digital payments, extending tokenisation requirements to recurring payments and offline transactions. The circular sets a Q2 2027 compliance deadline for payment aggregators and merchants handling stored card data to migrate to compliant token vaults. The directions also introduce stricter transaction authentication requirements for card-not-present transactions above ₹5,000 and mandate real-time fraud monitoring for all tokenised transactions.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.body: India's original tokenisation mandate (2022) already reshaped how every card payment works, but left gaps in recurring billing and offline transactions — exactly the flows where card data was most likely to be stored insecurely. This closure affects subscription businesses, insurance premium collection, EMI payments and any merchant using offline-capable POS terminals. The Q2 2027 deadline is tight for companies that built their recurring payment logic around raw card storage and retry mechanisms.

sections.heading: What to watch
sections.body: Monitor whether payment aggregators like Razorpay, PayU and Cashfree announce migration tools or timeline extensions. Track the impact on subscription businesses' payment success rates — the original tokenisation mandate caused a temporary dip in success rates before the ecosystem adapted. Watch for any RBI relaxation of the timeline if industry compliance runs behind schedule.
